README covers 4 concepts (funnel, context library, starter-not-loaf, streams in one line) and 13 commands: /bootstrap-repo and /tailor-ang in quick start, the funnel as a stage|question|command table, /raise-workflow-improvement and /improve-workflow for bending Ang; the rest goes to the docs site

knowns.fact: Requirements: clean simple design, light/dark defaulting to system, existing framework, Zac's voice, brief attribution
Where the brain dump describes how Ang works and the files differ, the files are truth (e.g. evidence tiers)
An "extends"-style shared config (e.g. a team's base ang.json) is the team answer to a configurable config path. Sent here to spike as a documented pattern, not built into Ang

Pages' built-in Jekyll (3.10, frozen; best docs theme Just the Docs) gives sidebar and search; Just the Docs follows system dark mode with one extra stylesheet link and no JS (spike). Starlight or VitePress on Pages via a ~37-line Actions workflow meet the brief for $0, at the cost of roughly yearly forced workflow bumps and framework breaking releases. Custom domain on Pages adds ~$10-12/yr; another host adds a vendor and no gain the brief asks for. Zac leans Pages; anything beyond it must justify its burden
knowns.answers: Hosting: what can GitHub Pages do on its own (built-in Jekyll, themes, plain Markdown) against the brief, and how does it compare with a framework on Pages or a domain plus hosting, in money and effort?

knowns.fact: Starlight 0.42.8 on Astro 7.4.5 builds first time in about 1.6s from 41 lines of config and code (32 without a link plugin only the spike needs); system light/dark with an Auto/Light/Dark switcher, sidebar, Pagefind search and on-this-page nav all built in. Attribution needs a 6-line footer override. Remark plugins need @astrojs/markdown-remark since Astro 7's new default Markdown engine. Deploy on Pages: a 31-line Actions workflow. No definition lists; callouts need :::note syntax. Zac: his favourite so far — the best design, and nav, search and a layout every developer knows are pluses — but the colours are ugly and would need real tinkering

Install is the one-liner curl -fsSL https://github.com/zacbraddy/ang/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh (or releases/download/{tag}/install.sh for a set version); prerequisite Node 26+ with npm/npx. The README carries it as the quick start and says nothing about the release process. No uninstall command: removing Ang by hand is a docs-site page

Effort bake-off (4 identical changes): VitePress worked first time on every task in about half the time (4 tries vs 7); Starlight's friction came from its Markdown pipeline (link plugin ignoring base, stale content cache, components forcing .mdx). Upkeep runs the other way: Starlight breaks often in small documented steps and is actively maintained; VitePress 1.x is frozen on unsupported Vite 5 with an unscheduled v2 migration
knowns.answers: Starlight or VitePress: which takes less effort to implement, maintain, extend and modify for this site? Covers recolouring each (neither measured), callout and definition-list handling, upgrade churn (Astro's breaking majors vs VitePress v2 still in alpha) and Pages deploy upkeep

knowns.fact: Platforms (install-upgrade-release d37): macOS, Linux and Windows through WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux), with the one-liner, Claude Code and Node 26 all inside WSL; install.sh stops under Git Bash, MSYS or Cygwin. Native Windows is untested, best effort, needs Git for Windows and a 6-step manual install (giget, settings merge, version write). The README install section carries a one-line WSL note; Quick start carries platforms and the native Windows steps, re-checked against shipped files at build

Design direction mapped (2026-11-17): measured dev-tool docs agree on 16px body, line-height 1.5–1.75, 65–80ch lines and 4px spacing steps, all within Starlight's defaults (16px, 1.75, 45rem, system fonts); typefaces have no consensus (system stack, Inter, Geist all ship); home pages put the install command near the top and show the product, docs-first homes skip social proof; Starlight's hero has no code slot and OG images need a plugin; Mermaid (astro-mermaid) is the diagram option that follows light/dark. AI-look markers beyond Anthropic's own list are single-source and unverified. Mapped, not chosen
knowns.answers: Wider design direction beyond colour (type, spacing, imagery, home-page layout): what do designers currently rate as modern and clean for developer-tool docs? Research it when planning makes concrete design decisions, so the findings are fresh

decisions.decision: README and site are one epic, with the README sequenced first so it ships without waiting on site research; the README links out to the site for depth (Zac, 2026-11-17)
Funnel shown as a one-row-per-stage table with every stage command — Zac's pick so readers can run a full loop from the README alone
Framework is Starlight — Zac's pick on looks, plus active maintenance and backing outweigh VitePress's cheaper changes, frozen base and unknown v2 migration

Commands docs as 5 grouped pages (one anchor per command). Why Ang is first principles plus credits; Zac's history and personal usage fail the user-value bar and survive only as a few lines on Home and Quick start (Zac, 2026-11-17)

Palette is Radix slate + jade (candidate 4): light bg #fcfcfd, text #1c2024, accent #208368; dark bg #111113, text #edeef0, accent #1fd8a4. Set via Starlight's --sl-color-* variables in customCss. Light accent sits right at AA (4.5:1), so any tint change needs a contrast re-check (Zac, 2026-11-17)

Typefaces are Geist for body and headings and Geist Mono for code, self-hosted from Fontsource and set via --sl-font, --sl-font-mono and Expressive Code's --ec-* font variables. Text size, line-height and width stay at Starlight's defaults (Zac, 2026-11-17)

Home is Starlight's splash template: hero with title, tagline and 2 buttons; the curl install one-liner in a terminal code block below it (no Hero override); a short what-it-does paragraph; LinkCards to Start here, Concepts and Commands. No social proof, no feature-card grid (Zac, 2026-11-17)
Diagrams use Mermaid via astro-mermaid, registered before Starlight, so they follow the light/dark switch (Zac, 2026-11-17)
